tldr: Three Chinese brands terminated Kylian Mbappe inside about 24 hours over a clip filmed in April, and one of them had launched him with an openly artificial-intelligence-generated advertisement and run generated images of him through the World Cup, all of which became as unusable as filmed footage the moment the deal ended.  Open every live talent contract this week and check whether it says anything about previously recorded material you have never seen, or about what happens to generated likeness when the relationship ends.

A Syracuse University survey of 989 United States adults who use a social or video platform weekly found 69.7 percent think it is fully acceptable for a creator to run their channel purely to maximise profit, while 64.7 percent think a creator who changes their content style to win a higher-paying sponsor has compromised their integrity.  Rewrite your next creator brief to specify the claim and nothing about style, pacing or shot list, because the audience objects to the edit rather than the invoice.

Major League Baseball went from 32 mostly paid creators and 115 pieces of content in 2024 to 130 unpaid creators and 1,150 pieces in 2025, lifting views from 48 million to more than 86 million, by moving the whole approval burden into the briefing and then leaving the creative alone.  Build the guardrail document that lets you say yes to a hundred creators instead of negotiating with ten, and invite on access rather than fee outside your top tier.

Only 11 percent of connected-television advertising requests name the programme, 93 percent carry only a genre label — a short text string the seller writes — and 35 percent of those labels disagree with the classification of the one firm that checked them, which counted 3,600 distinct labels in a two-hour window against an industry list of 704.  Require programme-level reporting as a condition of your next television-app order, and price anything without a programme name as untargeted inventory.

One agency puts premium streaming advertising at 43 dollars per thousand people reached before the 3 November election, up from 34 to 35, with YouTube up about 20 percent, and pre-emption clauses let stations bump a brand's spot for a political buyer entirely.  Ask your buyer today which of your spots carry pre-emption clauses and what the make-good is, then move what you can into the week of 4 November when the political money comes out of the auction.

LADbible's owner grew its direct branded-content sales and still lost 35 percent of its core profit on 106 million pounds of revenue while the platform advertising income underneath it halved, leaving the company owing more than it holds in cash.  Write down what share of your video income depends on a rate a platform sets rather than a contract with a named buyer, and model next year with that half cut in two.

A Thai esports final's peak audience rose 7.6 percent while its hours watched fell 17.78 percent because fewer channels carried it, and at a mobile final in Lahore co-casting — creators restreaming the official feed with their own commentary — took roughly half of all watch time across 455 broadcasting channels.  Contract average concurrent viewers as the measure on every live sponsorship, and ask specifically what share of watch time came from creators restreaming the feed and whether your branding appeared on those versions at all.
